questions.solution: \($\mathrm{Q}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{M}_{1} \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}, \mathrm{Q}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{M}_{2} \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}$\) as \($\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^{2}$\) So, \($\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{t}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{~g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}\right) \mathrm{t}_{1}^{2} \ldots \ldots \ldots($1)\) \($\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{t}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{~g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}\right) \mathrm{t}_{2}^{2} \ldots \ldots . .($2)\) given \($\mathrm{t}_{1}\lt \mathrm{t}_{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{1}^{2}\lt \mathrm{t}_{2}^{2}$\) \($\mathrm{So}, \frac{2 \mathrm{~h}}{\mathrm{~g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}}\lt \frac{2 \mathrm{~h}}{\mathrm{~g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}}$\) \($\mathrm{~g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}} \gt \mathrm{g}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}$\) \($\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}\lt \frac{\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{M}_{2}}$\) \(\Rightarrow $\mathrm{Q}_{2} \mathrm{M}_{1} \gt \mathrm{Q}_{1} \mathrm{M}_{2}$\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electrostatic field line leaves at an angle $\alpha$ from point charge ${q}_{1}$ and connects with point charge $- {q}_{2}$ at an angle $\beta$(${q}_{1}$ and ${q}_{2}$ are positive) see figure below. If ${q}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}{q}_{1}$ and $\alpha = 30 ° ,$ then
questions.solution:
Consider another symmetric field line below line joining centres of charges ${q}_{1}$ and ${q}_{2}$

In given situation, flux (field lines) leaving charge ${q}_{1}$ at a solid angle $2\alpha =$ flux terminating over charge ${q}_{2}$ at a solid angle $2\beta$.
Clearly, in given situation

We can say that, flux leaving charge ${q}_{1}$ through a cone of semi-vertical angle $\alpha =$ flux terminating on charge ${q}_{2}$ through a cone of semi-vertical angle $\beta$.

To calculate flux, we first find flux through an elemental ring of base of cone and then we integrate to get total flux.

Area of elemental ring,
$dA = 2\pirds = 2\piRsin\alpha \cdot Rd\alpha$

Flux through elemental ring $\left(E ‖ dA\right)$

$dϕ = \dfrac{kQ}{R2} \cdot 2\piR^{2}sin\alphad\alpha$

Total flux through base of cone

$ϕ = {∫}_{0}^{α}\dfrac{kQ}{R2} \cdot 2\piR^{2}sin\alphad\alpha$

$= kQ2\pi{∫}_{0}^{α}sin\alphad\alpha$

$ϕ = \dfrac{Q}{2{ε}_{0}} \cdot \left($1 - cos$\alpha\right)

So, equating flux of both cones, we get

\dfrac{q1}{2{ε}_{0}} \left($1 - $cos\alpha\right) = \dfrac{q2}{2{ε}_{0}}\left($1 - $cos\beta\right)

$⇒ {q}_{1} $\left(1 - cos\alpha\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}{q}_{1}\left(1 - cos\beta\right)$

Substituting $\alpha =30 °$ in above equation, we get

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - cos30 °\right) = 1 - cos\beta$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} \left($1 - $\dfrac{3}{2}\right) =$1 - $cos\beta

$⇒ $cos\beta =$1 - $\dfrac{2}{3}\left($1 - $\dfrac{3}{2}\right)

$⇒ $cos\beta \approx$0 . 9$

So, angle \beta is not more than $30 °$.

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two mutually perpendicular infinitely long straight conductors carrying uniformly distributed charges of linear densities ${λ}_{1}$ and ${λ}_{2}$ are positioned at a distance $r$ from each other.

Force between the conductors depends on $r$ as
questions.solution:
Consider the arrangement given,

Force on a differentiable length element $\left(dl\right)$ of conductor $2$ due to field of conductor $1$ is
$dF = {E}_{1}dq$

where, ${E}_{1} =$ field of wire $1$ at location of $dl$

This force can be resolved into components $dFcos\theta$ and $dFsin\theta$

net force is sum of all $dFcos\theta$ components, whereas $ΣdFsin\theta = 0$.
So, net force on conductor $2$ is
$F = ∫ dF = ∫ {E}_{1}dq$

Here,
${E}_{1} = \dfrac{2k{λ}_{1}}{R} = 2k{λ}_{1}$

$dq = {λ}_{2}dl$

$\dfrac{l}{r} = tan\theta$ and $\dfrac{r}{R} = cos\theta$

$⇒ dl = r{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

Also, $\theta$ varies from $\dfrac{- \pi}{2} to \dfrac{π}{2}$ for conductor $2$.

So, $F = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{2k{λ}_{1}}{rsec\theta} \cdot {λ}_{2} \cdot r{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$
$= 2k{λ}_{1}{λ}_{2}{∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}sec\thetad\theta$

As, ${∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}sec\thetad\theta = a$ constant

We can say that,

${F}_{net} = C \cdot {λ}_{1}{λ}_{2},$ where $C =$ some constant.

$∴ {F}_{net} ∝ r^{0}$

questions.q:
Consider a sphere of radius $R$ with unform charged density and total charge $Q .$ The electrostatic potential distribution inside the sphere is given by
$ϕ ( r ) = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}R}\left(a + b ( r / R{)}^{c}\right) .$ Note that the zero of potential is at infinity The values of $( a, b, c )$ are:
questions.solution:
Potential inside uniformly charged solid sphere is given by
$V = \dfrac{kQ}{2{R}^{3}}\left[3{R}^{2} - {r}^{2}\right]$

$= \dfrac{kQ}{R}\left[\dfrac{3{R}^{2}}{2{R}^{2}} - \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{2{R}^{2}}\right]$

$= \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{\in}_{0}R}\left[\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)}^{2}\right]$
Compare with given formula, i.e,
$\dfrac{Q}{4\pi{\in}_{0}R}\left[a + b{\left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)}^{C}\right]$
$a = \dfrac{3}{2}, b = - \dfrac{1}{2}, c = 2$

For static condition $\mathrm{E}=0$ in both of conductor $\therefore \phi$ through a Gaussian surface just under the surface of conductor $=0$ but as $\phi=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}$ is not valid
So $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}=0$ is not correct statement. Some charge will present insider bulk of conductor.

questions.q: The potential due to an electrostatic charge distribution is $V\left(r\right) = \dfrac{qe^{- \alphar}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r},$ where $\alpha$ is positive. The net charge within a sphere centred at the origin and of radius $1 / \alpha$ is
questions.solution:
Electric field due to given charge distribution is

$E = - \dfrac{dV}{dr} = - \dfrac{d}{dr}\dfrac{q{e}^{- \alphar}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r}$

$= \dfrac{- q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{d}{dr}\left(\dfrac{{e}^{- \alphar}}{r}\right)$

$= \dfrac{- q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\left(\dfrac{- \alphar{e}^{- \alphar} - {e}^{- \alphar}}{{r}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot {e}^{- \alphar} \cdot \left(\dfrac{\alphar + 1}{{r}^{2}}\right)$

Electric field at $r = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ is

$E\left(r = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right) = \dfrac{q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot {e}^{- \alpha \times \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left(\dfrac{\alpha \times \dfrac{1}{\alpha} + 1}{1 / {\alpha}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\left(q / e\right)}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot 2{\alpha}^{2}$

Flux through a sphere of radius $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ is

$ϕ = ∫ E \cdot dA$

For spherical distribution,
$E \cdot dA = EdAcos0 ° = EdA$
and $E =$ uniform.
So, we have

$∴ ϕ = E ∫ dA$

$= \dfrac{q / e}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot 2{\alpha}^{2} \cdot 4\pi{\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)}^{2}$

or $ϕ = \dfrac{2q}{{ε}_{0}e}$

From Gauss' law, we have $ϕ = \dfrac{{q}_{enclosed}}{{ε}_{0}}$

So, charge enclosed in given sphere is $\dfrac{2q}{e}$

questions.q: A charge $+ q$ is distributed over a thin ring of radius $r$ with line charge density $\lambda = q\sin^{2}\theta / \left(\pir\right). Note that the ring is in the $ XY$-plane and \theta is the angle made by $ r$ with the $X$-axis. The work done by the electric force in displacing a point charge $+ Q$ from the centre of the ring to infinity is$
options: equal to zero only, if the path is a straight line perpendicular to the plane of the ring
questions.solution:
As charge distribution is over a circle, potential due to charge over ring is 
$V = \dfrac{k}{r} . {q}_{total}$
where, ${q}_{total} = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{q\sin^{2}\theta}{\pir} \left( rd$\theta\right)
$= \dfrac{q}{π}{∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{1 - cos2\theta}{2} .$ d$\theta
$= $\dfrac{q}{π}{\left(\dfrac{θ}{2} - \dfrac{sin2\theta}{4}\right)}_{0}^{2\pi} =$ q$
So, potential at centre of ring $= V = $\dfrac{k{q}_{total}}{r}
$⇒ V = $\dfrac{kq}{r}
Also, work done in taking a charge $ Q$ from centre of ring to infinity $=$ potential energy of system
$= V $\cdot$ Q = $\dfrac{kqQ}{r} =\dfrac{qQ}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two masses ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ carry positive charges ${Q}_{1}$ and ${Q}_{2},$ respectively. They are dropped to the floor in a laboratory set up from the same height, where there is a constant electric field vertically upwards. ${M}_{1}$ hits the floor before ${M}_{2}$. Then,
questions.solution:
Time of fall $= \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{a\text{ret}}}$

Net acceleration of charged masses is
${a}_{net} = g - \dfrac{qE}{m}$
As, ${M}_{1}$ hits the floor before ${M}_{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{a1}} > \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{a2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{a1} > \dfrac{1}{a2}$

$⇒ {a}_{2} > {a}_{1}$

When reciprocal is taken in equality sign is reversed, then.
$g - \dfrac{{Q}_{1}E}{M1} > g - \dfrac{{Q}_{2}E}{M2}$

$⇒ - \dfrac{{Q}_{1}E}{M1} > - \dfrac{{Q}_{2}E}{M2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{Q}_{1}E}{M1} < \dfrac{{Q}_{2}E}{M2}$

Here, multiplication with - 1reverse sign of inequality.

So, $\dfrac{Q1}{M1} < \dfrac{Q2}{M2}$

or ${M}_{2}{Q}_{1} < {M}_{1}{Q}_{2}$

$⇒ {M}_{1}{Q}_{2} > {M}_{2}{Q}_{1}$
